newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriot in AIDS trial blames lover for negligence.
newsitem.headline: Cypriot in AIDS trial blames lover for negligence.

text.p: A Cypriot charged with giving his British lover the deadly AIDS virus on Wednesday admitted to having unprotected sex with her by mistake, but blamed her for his blunder.
"I insisted on putting on a condom because of my problem but she was against it," Pavlos Georgiou, who is HIV positive, testified to a Cypriot court on Wednesday.
"She had a weakness for free sex," the burly fisherman added, referring to 45-year-old divorcee Janette Pink, now dying of AIDS.

Georgiou, 40, from the south eastern coastal resort of Ayia Napa, has been charged by Cypriot authorities with negligently transmitting the HIV virus which causes Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome to Pink during an affair.

It is the first such case in Cyprus and its outcome could set an important legal precedent on how to handle allegations on the willfull or negligent transmission of the deadly virus from one person to another.

Georgiou, whose wife died of AIDS and whose youngest of four children is also HIV positive, has denied the charge. It carries a sentence of up to two years in jail or a 1,500 Cyprus pound fine, or both.

He says Pink was well aware of his condition before any physical relationship started, and that they only had unprotected sex once after both consumed considerable quantities of alcohol on Pink's birthday in April 1994.
"I wasn't myself," he shrugged with a touch of embarassment as his lawyer asked him to disclose details of the incident in a packed courtroom.
"She took the condom off me and sat on top of me.... It happened in no time at all. Because of the circumstances I couldn't control myself."
Pink found him irresistible, he said. "I can remember with certainty she said she never met a more attractive man," said the tanned and bearded Georgiou.
"Many times she would congratulate me because she used to think all men were the same. She said she never met anyone like me."
But Pink, from Basildon in Essex, has accused Georgiou of concealing from her the fact he had HIV, telling her his AIDS-stricken wife was dying of leukaemia.
She left Georgiou last year, returning to Britain for treatment after developing full-blown AIDS.
